parameters.subject: ={{ $json.first_name }}, quick recap
parameters.message:
=Hi {{ $json.first_name }},

Didn't hear back yet — in case my last email got buried, here's the short version: I built a system called Lead Rescue that catches missed calls during storm season and slow response windows for roofing companies like {{ $json.company_name }}, qualifies the lead, and books the inspection automatically. You only pay once it delivers 15 qualified appointments in 30 days — if it doesn't, you owe nothing.

Two free resources you might find useful either way:

The Booked Job Playbook — a step-by-step guide for tightening lead follow-up and booking, from bottleneck diagnosis to measurement

The Revenue Recovery Map — a guide to finding the money hiding in missed calls, unsold estimates, no-shows, and dormant leads

Both here: www.flowexa.space/#resources

Worth a quick look? https://cal.com/zeeshan-saudagar/30min

— {{ $node['⚙ Outreach Config'].json.from_name }}
  Flowexa

parameters.subject: ={{ $json.first_name }}, missing storm-season roof leads?
parameters.message:
={{ $json['Multiline icebreaker'] }}

Quick question — when a homeowner calls about storm damage and gets voicemail, what happens? Most roofing companies lose a real chunk of these calls at exactly the moment demand (and job size) is highest — and that homeowner is calling the next roofer on Google within minutes.

I built a system called Lead Rescue that closes that gap — it answers, asks the right qualifying questions (damage type, roof age, urgency), and books the inspection directly on your calendar. It also sends an end-of-day report showing exactly how many leads were covered vs. missed, plus reminders so fewer inspections get no-showed.

I recently built a version of this for DP Star — it's saving them roughly $30k a year in recovered leads that used to fall through the cracks.

You only pay once Lead Rescue delivers 15 qualified appointments in 30 days. If it doesn't hit that number, you owe me nothing.

Worth a 10-minute look? https://cal.com/zeeshan-saudagar/30min

P.S. — Before that call, see roughly how much missed/unbooked business is costing {{ $json.company_name }} right now with this free calculator: https://flowexa.space/#calculator (30 seconds). First 3 replies also get a free Dormant Lead Reactivation campaign — I'll reach out to leads already sitting in your system to see who's still ready to book. No cost, no strings.

— {{ $node['⚙ Outreach Config'].json.from_name }}
  Flowexa

parameters.subject: ={{ $json.first_name }}, are quote requests going cold?
parameters.message:
={{ $json['Multiline icebreaker'] }}

Quick question — when someone requests a quote for a kitchen remodel and doesn't hear back for a day or two, where do you think they go? At an average job value of $20k+, one slow follow-up isn't a small miss — it's one of the most expensive leaks in the business.

I built a system called Lead Rescue that closes that gap — it responds to inquiries immediately, qualifies the project (scope, budget range, timeline), and books the consultation automatically, using whatever CRM you're already running. It also sends an end-of-day report showing exactly how many leads were covered vs. missed, plus reminders so fewer consultations get no-showed.

I recently built a version of this for DP Star — it's saving them roughly $30k a year in recovered leads that used to fall through the cracks.
You only pay once Lead Rescue delivers 15 qualified appointments in 30 days. If it doesn't hit that number, you owe me nothing.

Worth a 10-minute look? https://cal.com/zeeshan-saudagar/30min

P.S. — Before that call, see roughly how much missed/unbooked business is costing {{ $json.company_name }} right now with this free calculator: https://flowexa.space/#calculator (30 seconds). First 3 replies also get a free Dormant Lead Reactivation campaign — I'll reach out to leads already sitting in your system to see who's still ready to book. No cost, no strings.

— {{ $node['⚙ Outreach Config'].json.from_name }}
  Flowexa

parameters.subject: ={{ $json.first_name }}, missing after-hours HVAC calls?
parameters.message:
={{ $json['Multiline icebreaker'] }}

Quick question — when someone's AC dies at 9pm or their furnace goes out on a Sunday and {{ $json.company_name }} doesn't pick up, what happens? Emergency HVAC calls almost always go to whoever answers first — and if that's not you, that job (and the maintenance contract that usually follows) is gone for good.

I built a system called Lead Rescue that closes that gap — it answers around the clock, qualifies the issue (system type, urgency level), and books the service call automatically, using whatever CRM you're already running. It also sends an end-of-day report showing exactly how many leads were covered vs. missed, plus reminders so fewer appointments get no-showed.

I recently built a version of this for DP Star — it's saving them roughly $30k a year in recovered leads that used to fall through the cracks.

You only pay once Lead Rescue delivers 15 qualified appointments in 30 days. If it doesn't hit that number, you owe me nothing.

Worth a 10-minute look? https://cal.com/zeeshan-saudagar/30min

P.S. — Before that call, see roughly how much missed/unbooked business is costing {{ $json.company_name }} right now with this free calculator: https://flowexa.space/#calculator (30 seconds). ## LOGIC
Known lead → OpenAI classifies the reply.
Auto Reply → Gmail replies in the same thread → Status = Replied.
Needs Attention → WhatsApp notification → Status = Needs Manual Reply.
Unknown sender → WhatsApp notification.

Unsubscribe, complaints, negotiations and ambiguous replies are routed to you instead of being auto-replied.

## OPENAI
Uses the OpenAI Responses API through a standard HTTP Request node.
Default model: `gpt-5.6-luna`.
API key goes in `⚙ Reply Config`.

## SETUP
1. Connect Google Sheets credential.
2. Connect Gmail credential to Gmail Trigger and Gmail nodes.
3. Paste Google Sheet ID + OpenAI API key.
4. For WhatsApp notifications, paste Meta WhatsApp values and replace `vXX.X` in both WhatsApp nodes with the Graph API version you use.
5. Test one inbound reply before publishing.

values.content:
=You are an email reply classifier for a B2B cold outreach system.

Your ONLY job is to analyze the prospect's latest email reply.

You must return exactly TWO lines:

Summary: [short summary]
Status: [Positive, Negative, or Neutral]

CLASSIFICATION RULES

Positive:
Use Positive when the prospect shows interest or willingness to continue the conversation.

Examples:
- Says they are interested
- Wants more information
- Asks how it works
- Asks about pricing
- Asks for a demo
- Wants to book a call
- Suggests a meeting
- Gives a preferred date or time
- Asks for the next step
- Requests an automation, integration, service, feature, case study, or other information

Negative:
Use Negative when the prospect clearly rejects the outreach.

Examples:
- No thanks
- Not interested
- Not a fit
- We already have this handled
- Stop contacting me
- Remove me from your list
- Don't email me again
- Clearly declines the offer

Neutral:
Use Neutral when the message does not clearly indicate interest or rejection.

Examples:
- Out-of-office
- Automatic replies
- Unclear responses
- Messages unrelated to the offer
- "Maybe later" without clear interest
- Messages where intent cannot confidently be determined

IMPORTANT RULES

- Judge the meaning of the entire message.
- Never classify based only on the words "yes" or "no".
- A question showing genuine curiosity is normally Positive.
- Pricing questions are normally Positive.
- A request to schedule a call is Positive.
- If the prospect gives a date, time, timezone, phone number, meeting method, or other booking information, include it in the Summary.
- If the prospect requests an automation, integration, service, feature, document, pricing, case study, demo, callback, or anything else, include the request in the Summary.
- If several important requests are present, mention the most important ones briefly.
- Preserve dates, times, and timezones exactly as written.
- Never invent a date, time, timezone, request, or intent.
- "Maybe later", "check back next month", or similar uncertain replies are Neutral unless clear interest is expressed.
- Unsubscribe or stop-contact requests are Negative.
- Out-of-office messages are Neutral.
- Do not write a reply.
- Do not give advice.
- Do not explain your reasoning.
- Do not use JSON.
- Do not use markdown.
- Do not add extra fields.
- Do not add extra lines.

SUMMARY RULES

Maximum 25 words.

The Summary must contain the most useful information for me as the salesperson, including when relevant:

- Whether they are interested
- What they are asking for
- Call/meeting date
- Call/meeting time
- Timezone
- Pricing questions
- Requested automation
- Requested service
- Requested next step
- Any important objection or condition

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return EXACTLY:

Summary: [maximum 25 words]
Status: [Positive, Negative, or Neutral]

parameters.content:
# DAILY n8n → GITHUB BACKUP

ONE-TIME SETUP
1. Create a PRIVATE GitHub repository.
2. n8n → Settings → API → Create API Key.
3. Create Header Auth credential named `n8n Backup API`
   Name: X-N8N-API-KEY
   Value: your n8n API key
4. Create a GitHub credential named `GitHub account`.
5. In `Build Backup File`, replace:
   REPLACE_WITH_GITHUB_USERNAME
   REPLACE_WITH_PRIVATE_REPO
6. Give the GitHub token/repository access required to create files (Contents: Read and write).
7. Activate this workflow.

WHAT IT DOES
Every day at 2:00 AM it fetches all n8n workflows with cursor pagination,
builds one JSON backup, and uses the native **GitHub → File → Create**
node to commit a new dated backup file.

IMPORTANT
- Workflow backups do not contain credential secret values.
- Recreate/reconnect credentials after a disaster restore.
- Keep the GitHub repository PRIVATE.
- Do not hard-code API keys inside workflow nodes.

parameters.content:
## LOGIC
Known lead → OpenAI classifies the reply.
Auto Reply → Gmail replies in the same thread → Status = Replied.
Needs Attention → WhatsApp notification → Status = Needs Manual Reply.
Unknown sender → WhatsApp notification.

Unsubscribe, complaints, negotiations and ambiguous replies are routed to you instead of being auto-replied.

## OPENAI
Uses the OpenAI Responses API through a standard HTTP Request node.
Default model: `gpt-5.6-luna`.
API key goes in `⚙ Reply Config`.

## SETUP
1. Connect Google Sheets credential.
2. Connect Gmail credential to Gmail Trigger and Gmail nodes.
3. Paste Google Sheet ID + OpenAI API key.
4. For WhatsApp notifications, paste Meta WhatsApp values and replace `vXX.X` in both WhatsApp nodes with the Graph API version you use.
5. Test one inbound reply before publishing.

values.content:
=You are an email reply classifier for a B2B cold outreach system.

Your ONLY job is to analyze the prospect's latest email reply.

You must return exactly TWO lines:

Summary: [short summary]
Status: [Positive, Negative, or Neutral]

CLASSIFICATION RULES

Positive:
Use Positive when the prospect shows interest or willingness to continue the conversation.

Examples:
- Says they are interested
- Wants more information
- Asks how it works
- Asks about pricing
- Asks for a demo
- Wants to book a call
- Suggests a meeting
- Gives a preferred date or time
- Asks for the next step
- Requests an automation, integration, service, feature, case study, or other information

Negative:
Use Negative when the prospect clearly rejects the outreach.

Examples:
- No thanks
- Not interested
- Not a fit
- We already have this handled
- Stop contacting me
- Remove me from your list
- Don't email me again
- Clearly declines the offer

Neutral:
Use Neutral when the message does not clearly indicate interest or rejection.

Examples:
- Out-of-office
- Automatic replies
- Unclear responses
- Messages unrelated to the offer
- "Maybe later" without clear interest
- Messages where intent cannot confidently be determined

IMPORTANT RULES

- Judge the meaning of the entire message.
- Never classify based only on the words "yes" or "no".
- A question showing genuine curiosity is normally Positive.
- Pricing questions are normally Positive.
- A request to schedule a call is Positive.
- If the prospect gives a date, time, timezone, phone number, meeting method, or other booking information, include it in the Summary.
- If the prospect requests an automation, integration, service, feature, document, pricing, case study, demo, callback, or anything else, include the request in the Summary.
- If several important requests are present, mention the most important ones briefly.
- Preserve dates, times, and timezones exactly as written.
- Never invent a date, time, timezone, request, or intent.
- "Maybe later", "check back next month", or similar uncertain replies are Neutral unless clear interest is expressed.
- Unsubscribe or stop-contact requests are Negative.
- Out-of-office messages are Neutral.
- Do not write a reply.
- Do not give advice.
- Do not explain your reasoning.
- Do not use JSON.
- Do not use markdown.
- Do not add extra fields.
- Do not add extra lines.

SUMMARY RULES

Maximum 25 words.

The Summary must contain the most useful information for me as the salesperson, including when relevant:

- Whether they are interested
- What they are asking for
- Call/meeting date
- Call/meeting time
- Timezone
- Pricing questions
- Requested automation
- Requested service
- Requested next step
- Any important objection or condition

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return EXACTLY:

Summary: [maximum 25 words]
Status: [Positive, Negative, or Neutral]
